old: he thought he would have run away from her.
new: he thought he would run away from her.
reason: The certainty repair restored 'he thought', but 'would have run' after the present-tense condition 'if she kept staring' is a tense clash. 'Would run' keeps the hedge and matches 'kept'.

old: it must be for some kind of strongbox, and that perhaps everything was hidden there
new: it must be for some kind of strongbox, and perhaps everything was hidden there
reason: The certainty repair ('and that perhaps everything was hidden there') restored the source's 'perhaps' but left a dangling 'that' after the dash-interrupted clause. Dropping 'that' keeps the hedge. Folds in accessibility item 0.

old: He said a couple of words in French with a foreigner
new: He said a couple of words in French to a foreigner
reason: The invention repair removed 'even exchanged' but kept its preposition: 'said ... with a foreigner' is unidiomatic. The source has 'said a couple of words in French to a foreigner'.
A listener cannot tell that Gambrinus's is a tavern; one word locates it.
Casual modern 'weird' jars in an 1860s voice; 'odd' does the same job.

'Workout' is a twentieth-century gym word that breaks the period world. [verifier-modified: The source has 'My word, he has been going it!', which is slang for drinking or living fast: the sweat-soaked man is taken for a drunk. 'Workout' is anachronistic, but 'hard at it' suggests he has been working. 'On a spree' keeps the drunkenness.]

old: people of every sort and both genders
new: people of every sort and both sexes
reason: 'Both genders' is modern usage; 'both sexes' is the period phrase.
Heard aloud next to 'Mr. Captain', 'his honor' sounds like the officer, not the drunken writer.

old: his sentimental outburst to Ilya Petrovitch
new: his sentimental outburst in front of Ilya Petrovitch
reason: He addressed Nikodim Fomitch, not Ilya Petrovitch, so 'to' misstates who he spoke to.

old: but withdrew the moment he came to
new: but withdrew the moment Raskolnikov came to
reason: The two 'he's make it sound as if Ilya Petrovitch had fainted and come to.

old: even when he had decided in the night, without hesitation
new: even when he had decided in the night to throw it all in the water, without hesitation
reason: The listener is not told what he decided, so the sentence loses its object.

old: So I haven't come to Razumihin on purpose?
new: Why, I've come to Razumihin's without meaning to!
reason: The negative question reads backwards on first hearing; the thought is that he arrived without intending to. [verifier-modified: The source has 'why, I have not come to Razumihin of my own accord!'. That is an exclamation of discovery, and his doubt only follows it ('have I come on purpose or...'). The proposed question weakens the assertion, so keep the exclamation and the 'Why,'. The meaning 'without meaning to' is right.]

old: Rousseau was a kind of Radishchev.
new: Rousseau was a kind of Radishchev, our Russian radical.
reason: Radishchev is obscure to an English listener and the joke depends on knowing he was a radical writer.
